page: Vultr voc-g-8c-32gb-160s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server powered by an AMD EPYC processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core, running at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The processor includes 16 MB of L3 cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 KB of L1d cache. Memory capacity is 32.0 GB, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is provided by a 160 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core performance, with the server placing in the top 25% for stress-ng single-core CPU tests and Geekbench single-core scores. Multi-core performance is average, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 9919.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 18127.64. Memory bandwidth is stable, yielding 117.03 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 77.42 GB/sec for uncached large-block writes. The server demonstrates average capabilities in database operations, showing 15.29 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks and a static web serving throughput of 8.45 GB/sec.

While the server handles lightweight LLM tasks adequately, such as prompt processing for a small 135M model at 656.07 tokens per second, it exhibits a performance bottleneck on larger models. Prompt processing for a medium 7B model falls into the bottom 25% at 18.38 tokens per second. Given these performance characteristics and the balanced resource allocation, this server is well-suited for general-purpose workloads, software compilation, text processing, and moderate database operations, rather than heavy LLM inference or memory-intensive computing.
